overview: This Senate resolution designates April 20 through 26, 2026, as National Dark Sky Week. It notes that artificial light at night, often called light pollution, can hide the stars, disrupt wildlife and waste energy, while dark skies support stargazing, tourism, science and education. The resolution encourages federal agencies to coordinate on expanding dark sky opportunities, encourages communities and educators to raise awareness, and urges people and organizations to use responsible outdoor lighting, such as shielded, downward-facing lights. It is ceremonial and does not create any new rules. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on April 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say simple lighting changes can protect the night sky, help wildlife and save energy, and a national week raises awareness of those benefits.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
